bull.b: Zeta's ~ $200M TTM free cash flow with rising OCF demonstrates durable cash conversion despite GAAP losses. Robust FCF funds R&D, product rollouts, M&A and buybacks, lowers refinancing risk, and supports multi-period investments in AI and sales capacity over the next several quarters.

TTM zero debt and a larger equity base materially improve financial flexibility. Low leverage lets management prioritize growth investments, M&A integration (Marigold), and product buildout without elevated default risk, providing structural resilience across varying market conditions.

bull.t: Proprietary data/AI moat and customer expansion
bull.b: Zeta's SuperGraph identity assets plus fast Athena adoption create a durable competitive edge: higher ARPU, vendor consolidation wins, and increased multi-use customers. This strengthens retention, upsell economics and sustainable revenue expansion as clients embed Zeta across channels.

bear.b: Despite operational momentum, Zeta remains GAAP loss-making. Ongoing net losses keep ROE negative and mean reported profitability is contingent on continued margin and cost improvements. Failure to sustain adjusted margins risks delaying durable GAAP profitability restoration.

bear.t: Rising cost of revenue / mix pressure
bear.b: Higher-cost social and agency-driven revenue increased cost of goods sold by 190bps. If the business mix stays skewed toward higher-cost channels, gross margins could be structurally constrained, requiring sustained scale or efficiency gains to preserve margin expansion.

Agency payment timing creates material working-capital variability (~13-point FCF headwind), a structural cash conversion risk for the agency-heavy portions of the business. Recurring timing mismatches can limit short-term reinvestment capacity and require active treasury management.
